issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String attribute, but the solution implementation changes the attribute type to a custom LectureName class. This deviates from the specified attribute types and introduces type mismatches in getters/setters (e.g., getLectureName() returning/using different types), which will confuse students and prevent a straightforward mapping from the spec/template to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution follow the problem specification: change the lectureName attribute back to type String (private String lectureName), update the constructor and all getters/setters to use String, and remove or do not rely on the LectureName class. Alternatively, if LectureName is intentionally required, update the problem statement, UML and template to specify LectureName instead of String and make getters/setters and constructor signatures consistent.

issues.description: The UML and problem statement require a constructor that initializes attributes including lectureName (String) in a specific order, but the solution constructor signature expects a LectureName object instead of a String. This mismatch in constructor parameter types/ordering conflicts with the specified design and with what students will implement from the template/spec.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution constructor with the problem/template by changing its first parameter to String lectureName and preserving the attribute order from the UML. If the custom LectureName type is required pedagogically, update the problem statement and template to document the LectureName type and show the expected constructor signature accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template specify the lectureName attribute as a String, but the solution introduces a new LectureName class and makes the Lecture.lectureName field and constructor accept a LectureName object. This changes the expected type/identifier for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and can confuse students when mapping the UML/requirements to the provided implementation and constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the lecture name across all artifacts. Either: (a) revert the solution to use a String for the lectureName field and constructor (matching the UML and template), and remove the LectureName class; or (b) update the problem statement and template to require a LectureName type everywhere (and document the reason), ensuring constructor signatures, getters, and setters consistently use LectureName.
